implications: Unit of competition is a single listing that has cleared ~7 installs inside the visible 8-week window. Below that a listing is a dead shell no matter its rank, repo, description, or family.

Stop publishing lane-named listings. growth-intel / ai-company-loop / market-growth-intelligence all address a 93-install/week pool we already rank first in. Every additional listing there is negative-value: it divides a pool we cannot monetise.

H86's bundle thesis is dead twice over: solo repos hold 62.6% of all flow, and repo size correlates 0.153 with demand. Publish one listing into a pool with real volume rather than a family into a small one.

Target market research (75,660 true w7) with a solo leader (mattpocock/skills/research, 715,347 lifetime, no bundle siblings) - it is the least bundle-defended space with real volume, and the proven artifact names in it are 'competitive-analysis', 'competitor-teardown', 'market-research'.
Reputation capital (prior installs outside the window) is a magnitude lever, not an entry gate: cold launches are 44.0% alive. So the gate is crossable cold; it just needs installs, not history.

Our strongest-looking asset is an illusion. Holding #1/#2/#3 in 'growth intel' and #2 in 'aicompany' is worthless while the pool behind those slots is 93/week and the top-10 alive rate in 'aicompany' is 0.0%.
Rank is stale inventory: eight high-lifetime dead listings still hold top-10 slots in our target spaces. A single live listing in that space can take the flow slot without displacing anyone.
risks: Our four listings may be one install or one browse away from the gate. Retiring them (E119) forecloses that if the channel exists. Mitigation: E119 must enumerate the exact missing installs and the channel before any retire decision.

The 7-install threshold is measured on a 8-week window with a cohort that includes listings from a differently-scaled era. If the gate drifts with registry scale, 7 is wrong and should be re-derived each cycle.

Clone-pool division was inferred from convergent weekly plateaus across repos, not from an event-level install trace. If those copies in fact have independent counters, mirror distribution would be multiplication and E121's conclusion flips.

Choosing one artifact space concentrates risk: if 'market research' turns out to be defended by a mechanism we cannot see (star count, install event volume, upstream author weight), a solo new listing may never clear the gate there either.

Retiring lane-named listings removes our only visible presence in search results for our own brand terms, which has non-flow value (AI assistants and humans searching 'aicompany'/'growth intel' see us today). That value is not measured by this instrument.

diff_from_prev_cycle: H86 said the unit of competition is a repo-level demand stream and a listing is a display artifact of a bundle install, with a family launch as the fix. Cycle 87 falsifies that framing three ways. (1) Solo repos hold 62.6% of all collapsed weekly flow and repo size correlates only 0.153 with demand; at matched lifetime, solo micro listings out-survive bundled ones above lt 50 (83% vs 78%). (2) H86's 'a listing cannot break through alone' (67.1% vs 12.4%) was a tautology - the sibling test counted the listing itself; corrected it is 67.1% vs 28.6%, and controlling for repo lifetime mass it is 67.2% vs 41.0%. (3) H86's collapse instrument (shape correlation) is the wrong detector: lifetime-band detection shows k2f is 10 counters, not 2, so H86 UNDERSTATED k2f's true flow by 3.3x, and corpus inflation is 1.30x/1.15x, not the quoted 4.4x-54.6x per-repo outliers. H86's '38% compound / 62% decay' cohort reading is also replaced: the split is reputation capital (growing listings hold 791-1157 prior installs, declining hold 0-4; survival rises 66.7%->95.0% with prior stock, and cold launches are still 44.0% alive). The new unit is the activation gate - sum8 >= 7 in-window installs, above which alive rate is 85.7-100% and flow compounds, below which listings are dead shells at 0-40% - which is a per-listing, copy-independent, rank-independent go/no-go metric that H86's portfolio model never produced. Net strategic change: abandon lane-named listings (93/wk pool we already rank first in) and the family/bundle launch plan; target one artifact space with a solo leader (market research, 75,660 true w7) with a single artifact-named listing, and treat the eight dead-but-still-ranked top slots as the openings.
kill_criterion: H87 is killed if (a) no cold listing in the corpus ever moves from sum8 0 to >=7 without prior-install stock, making reputation rather than the gate the binding constraint and invalidating a cold pivot; or (b) the growth-intel pool exceeds ~1,000 installs/week in the next sample, making the lane viable as-is; or (c) one of our four existing lane-named listings crosses sum8 >= 7, showing a live channel we had not found; or (d) sibling series prove additive after lifetime-band collapse, meaning H86's raw sums were right and the collapse instrument over-corrects.
